AnswerBriefJson.description:
An answer with no packet set in its ingress and its branches. The
summary parts keep their packet sets, because each part is a set.

BranchBriefJson.description:
A branch with its verdict, its delay, the number of its steps and, in
the form `steps`, one line for each step.

reads.description: The data that the claim reads.

scopes.description: The scopes on which the claim runs: `twin`, `devices` or `query`.

ClaimOut.description: The result of a claim on a scope.
ClaimOut.title: ClaimOut

ClaimResult.description: The result of a claim or of one evidence row.

refers_to.description: The table and the column that a value refers to.

semantic.description: The meaning of the values, for example `device`, `interface`, `vrf`.

top.description:
The most frequent values with their counts, at most 5, the most
frequent first.

ColumnType.description: The type of the values of a column.

oneOf.description: An address with a prefix length.

Counts.description: The number of evidence rows of each result.

EncapJson.description: An encapsulation header. The values are field values.

provenance.description: The source spans of the data: file:first-last.

subject.description: What the row is about, for example a link or a branch.

Field_string.description: A header field value: {"known": value}, {"in": [...]}, "unknown", "absent" or "original".

Field_uint16.description: A header field value: {"known": value}, {"in": [...]}, "unknown", "absent" or "original".

Field_uint32.description: A header field value: {"known": value}, {"in": [...]}, "unknown", "absent" or "original".

Field_uint8.description: A header field value: {"known": value}, {"in": [...]}, "unknown", "absent" or "original".

oneOf.description: The verdicts, the parts and the branches with no trace steps.
The summary, and one line for each trace step, with no packet sets.
The full answer with each packet set.

FragmentName.description: The fragment state of a request.

inner.description: The inner header of an encapsulated current header.

IcmpName.description: The name of an ICMP echo type.

IcmpTypeArg.description:
An ICMP type: a number, or the name of the echo request or the echo
reply.

IngressBriefJson.description: The ingress of one run, with no packet set.

IngressJson.description:
The ingress of one run of the answer: the packets of the run and the
interface where they enter, or the reason why the ingress is not known.

PacketSetJson.description:
A packet set: its members. A member is a product of field values. The
members are disjoint and in the fixed order of the bit table.

PathBriefOut.description: A path answer in the form `summary` or `steps`.
PathBriefOut.title: PathBriefOut

PathQueryArgs.description:
The fields of a path query. A field that the query does not state is
not known.

destination.mac.description: The destination MAC address: 6 hexadecimal bytes with colons.

form.description: The form of the answer. The default is summary.

ingress.description:
The ingress point as <device>/<interface>. Without it, the
attachment records of the source address give the ingress.

l2_priority.description: The layer 2 priority. It needs network.vlan.id.

network.transport.description: The protocol name. Give network.iana_number or network.transport.

reply.description: Run the reply. The default is true.

source.mac.description: The source MAC address: 6 hexadecimal bytes with colons.

tcp_flags.description: The TCP flags that are set.

topology.description:
A built-in topology, or `store` for the newest snapshot of the store
of the server.

PathQueryArgs.title: PathQueryArgs

Problem.description: A problem object of RFC 9457 with the rsim error code.

QueryEcho.description:
The query input in the JSON output. Each field is there, and a field
that is not given is `null`. The protocol is a number and has its name
if it has one, the ICMP type is a number, and the TCP flags are in the
order of their bits with no repeat.

QueryJson.description: The query input of an output: of a path query or of a set query.

ReplyBriefJson.description: The reply of a delivered branch in a brief form.

SetArg.description:
A set: an address, a prefix, a number, a range such as 1-1023, or a
comma list. A field that is not given has all values.

SetBriefOut.description: A set answer in the form `summary` or `steps`.
SetBriefOut.title: SetBriefOut

SetEcho.description:
The set query input in the JSON output. Each field is the normalized
text of its set, or `null` if it is not given.

SetItem.description: One item of a set list.

SetQueryArgs.description:
The fields of a set query. Each field takes a set. A field that is not
given has all values.

form.description: The form of the answer. The default is summary.

ingress.description:
The ingress point as <device>/<interface>. Without it, the
attachment records of the source addresses give the ingress.

reply.description: Run the replies. The default is true.

tcp_flags.description: The TCP flag values: numbers, ranges, or flag names joined with +.

topology.description:
A built-in topology, or `store` for the newest snapshot of the store
of the server.

SetQueryArgs.title: SetQueryArgs

StepLineJson.description: One trace step with no packet set.

SummarizeOut.description: The counts of a table and of each column.
SummarizeOut.title: SummarizeOut

key.description: The key columns, which give the default order of the rows.

needs.description: The data that the table needs, so a client knows why it is empty.

next_cursor.description: The cursor of the next page, or `null` on the last page.

total.description: The number of rows that match the filters, on all pages.

branches.description: In a path drawing: the branches that cross the edge.

claims.description: The result of each requested claim on the edge.

facts.description:
The facts of the edge, for example the speed and the duplex of both
ends of a link, or the tunnels of an overlay edge, each with its
encapsulation function, its source, its peer and its VNIs.

layer.description:
`physical`, `overlay` or `function`; in a path drawing also
`underlay` for a hop of an encapsulated packet.

overlay.description: In a path drawing: the overlay edge of an underlay edge.

provenance.description: The source spans of the facts: file:first-last.

functions.description: The number of functions of a device node.

TopologyOut.description: The topology of a twin, or the drawing of the paths of a query.
TopologyOut.title: TopologyOut

TwinJson.description: The twin that gave an answer.

base.description: The identifier of the base: a built-in topology or a snapshot.

layers.description: The what-if layers on the base, in order. Empty with no scenario.

snapshot.description: The snapshot cycle of the base, or `null` for a built-in topology.

UniformJson.description: A QoS header field over the members of a set: {"value": field value}, "varies" or "none".

UniqueOut.description: The distinct values of columns with their counts.
UniqueOut.title: UniqueOut

kind.description:
`deliver`, `exit`, `drop` or `unknown`. `exit`: the packets left the
twin on an edge interface, which the reason names.

rsim.description: Not checked yet: the server listens only on a loopback address. The scope rsim.scenario.write is for the what-if scenarios.

scopes.rsim.read: Read the twins, the tables, the queries and the claims.

info.description: The REST API of the rsim network digital twin. Each table, query and claim is below its twin. GraphQL, Cypher and gRPC are not used.
info.title: rsim

post.summary: The Model Context Protocol through its Streamable HTTP transport, revision 2026-07-28: one JSON-RPC message in the body; the headers MCP-Protocol-Version, Mcp-Method and, for tools/call, Mcp-Name must agree with it. A request gets its response; a notification gets 202. The tools are the tools of rsim-mcp.
